anthology-v9-0285.text: Will Bed Common : general, public, widespread LAW, COMMON. The common law is that which derives its force and authority from the universal consent and immemorial practice of the people. It has never received the sanction of the legislature, by an express act, which is the criterion by which it is distinguished from the statute law. It has never been reduced to writing; by this expression, however, it is not meant that all those laws are at present merely oral, or communicated from former ages to the present solely by word of mouth, but that the evidence of our common law is contained in our books of Reports, and depends on the general practice and judicial adjudications of our courts. In some states the English common law has been adopted by statute. There is no general rule to ascertain what part of the English common law is valid and binding. To run the line of distinction, is a subject of embarrassment to courts, and the want of it a great perplexity to the student. Kirb. Rep. Pref. It may, however, be observed generally, that it is binding where it has not been superseded by the constitution of the United States, or of the several states, or by their legislative enactments, or varied by custom, and where it is founded in reason and consonant to the genius and manners of the people.

The corporation, when acting as trustee, can complete any document for the benefit of the trust as 'For and on behalf of the Board of Trustees.' Use it as a device to create the perception of credibility/status & a big stick to keep away pirates etc To use the example of the tax department, or banks etc: How often do you see a name, or how often do you see a title? Usually you see something like 'Compliance Officer', 'Customer Services Manager' 'Deputy Commissioner' etc etc and a copy & pasted signature that doesn't correspond to a name. Play by the same rules, leave something nebulous like 'For and on behalf of the board of trustees' with an unintelligible squiggle instead of a signature and in my experience, you get left alone. The perception you want to create is that the trust is a huge organisation, wielding massive power and assets, with a team of lawyers to mess up anyone who tries to screw with trust property.
